900015646152.desc: This is a Winfield Pasadena porcelain vase in the Art Deco mode. It has a creamy white matte glaze exterior with subtle surface texture and smooth turquoise interior. It is a sophisticated design with side ribbing and a sea-blue interior which works with almost all interiors from Art Deco, Craftsman Style, MidCentury Modern and Modern! The Winfield Pottery Company began in 1929 in Pasadena, California and continued production until 1962. It manufactured hand-crafted, vitrified china and other items, including ceramic ware, artware, vases, and accessories. The ceramics are well-known for their mid-century modern style shapes and hand-painted designs. "Winfield Pasadena" mark indicates an early piece from the Pasadena location, often marked "Winfield Pasadena". Early studio pottery is rarer and more sought after than later mass-produced wares. The “Winfield Pasadena” mark identifies it as having been produced by the original Winfield Pottery in Pasadena, California, between 1929 and 1946. (After 1946, the pottery's production was split between different makers, resulting in variations on the original mark.) The vase is a rare and original piece of art and a collectors item. This art deco vase from Winfield is a fine example of craftsmanship from Pasadena. Its elegant shape and subdued colors show a timeless sophistication. Winfield Pottery of Pasadena was founded by Lesley Winfield Sample in 1929. Sample was born in England in 1897 where he received instruction in ceramics. He immigrated to Southern California in the 1920s. The original site began as a studio and School of Clayworking and offered classes. Sample managed to turn out an exceptional line of cast porcelain vases and bowls. Pieces were fired only once at 1950°F, in a small muffle kiln, where clay body and glaze matured simultaneously.
